speaker: hamnet_sadler
text: Step in out of the sun, Will. The second batch of penny maslin is just coming off the peel.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Thou hast the batch, and I have ash on me up to the cuff. Thy cousin has his twenty shillings toward the oak.

speaker: hamnet_sadler
text: Then the beam can be spoken of after the loaves. Stand clear of the peel.

speaker: richard_quiney
text: I followed you from the row. Not for the town, this time. My own malt-house wants two pounds, to carry it to Michaelmas.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Two pounds. Yes.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Will.

speaker: judith_sadler
text: Say the word, Master Quiney. Gift, loan or purchase? I'll not have it called friendship afterwards and nobody knowing which.

speaker: richard_quiney
text: A loan.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: A loan.

speaker: judith_sadler
text: And when does it come home, and what use does it carry on its back?

speaker: richard_quiney
text: A pound by Martinmas or soon after. The rest by Lady Day following.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: And no use upon it. I will not take use.

speaker: richard_quiney
text: I will not offer it. You to me, and no interest between us.

speaker: judith_sadler
text: Loan, then. A pound by Martinmas or soon after, the rest by Lady Day, and no use. I have heard it, and the oven has heard it.

speaker: hamnet_sadler
text: That is the first honest bargain made in my shop this year, and I include my own.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Forty shillings on the board. The word is already said, so the silver can follow it.

speaker: richard_quiney
text: I am lighter for the word than for the silver. I know which it is, now, and I will not call it a gift at Christmas.

speaker: judith_sadler
text: Bring the three children on Sunday after the sermon instead of thy purse, and I will have a shoulder of mutton in the bread oven and a pie with a crust for them.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: We will come on Sunday after morning prayer, Judith.

speaker: hamnet_sadler
text: Sunday, if thou art minded to argue with a baker, argue after the mutton. The peel is hot today, and I am not thy clerk.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will not argue a baker on a Thursday. The pie is the kinder bill.

speaker: judith_sadler
text: Then the pie is promised, and the forty shillings are a loan, and I will not have the two stories folded into one.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: That's two pounds you know where it is.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: In the belt until this minute, and in the book tonight as its own line. The timber was a different line.

speaker: judith_sadler
text: Write the word you both said, or I have kept a bakehouse for nothing.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Come home and write it. The street has had enough of our sums for one Thursday.

speaker: hamnet_sadler
text: Sunday, then. Mutton, and a pie, and no purse in place of the children.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Sunday. The three of them have been promised, and I will not unpromise a pie.
